themes.title: Safety disclosures and the slowdown rift
themes.summary: OpenAI publicly disclosed six model-misbehavior incidents and a new framework for tracking and reporting them, as the industry's safety push moves from rhetoric to process. The pause movement is now bipartisan in Washington and real inside the labs: FT reports staff at OpenAI and Anthropic are fighting over whether to act on slowdown talk, while DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg warns AI must not outrun safety controls.
themes.angle: Boards should treat 'slowing down' as a governance demand, not a tech debate — expect procurement, insurance and disclosure questions soon.

themes.title: Agentic AI: funding and monetization accelerate
themes.summary: Agentic AI is where the money is concentrating: Manus is doubling to $4B in its first round since Beijing forced it out of Meta, and agent startup Instinct is reportedly in talks at a $10B valuation. OpenAI is simultaneously commercializing agents through 'Sponsored Agents' and advertiser tools, while Salesforce and Apple push enterprise agentic and infrastructure bets.
themes.angle: The agentic layer is separating into funded platforms, distribution and enterprise plumbing — watch who owns the agent's 'actions' contract.

themes.title: AI capex politics: power, rates, chips
themes.summary: Washington took its most significant step on AI infrastructure costs — a bipartisan House vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act to shield consumers from AI-era power bills — while the Fed's first hike since 2023 changes the funding math for datacenter buildouts. The chip-map keeps shifting: Huawei prepares an Nvidia challenger this week, Modi opens a $30B semiconductor push, and Holtec shelved its IPO citing 'perfect storm' sentiment against datacenters.
themes.angle: Inference economics is now a public-policy issue: power pricing, rate hikes and chip sovereignty move from tech columns to finance and risk committees.

themes.title: Gulf shadow AI: adoption outpacing controls
themes.summary: The region's fastest-moving AI story is the gap between adoption and governance: AGBI reports Gulf companies exposed to 'shadow AI' as staff use unauthorized tools ahead of controls, and Microsoft UAE's Amr Kamel flags agentic AI rewriting the cybersecurity equation. Saudi leadership is leaning into governance diplomacy — the Saudi AI chief pressed for turning 'shared principles into action' at UNESCO, alongside the Riyadh Forum on governing rapidly advancing AI.
themes.angle: Gulf boards face a compliance dilemma the global newsletters ignore: adoption velocity is a competitive asset and a liability at the same time.

themes.title: GCC AI infrastructure after the war
themes.summary: The spring Iran strikes are still reshaping GCC AI infrastructure: the UAE is revising its AI datacenter plan, Amazon's AWS facilities in Bahrain and the UAE remain unrestored, and Washington is counting billions in damage to Gulf assets. The response is diplomatic and capital-heavy — Abu Dhabi signed AI/datacenter MOUs with seven Korean companies, and the UAE and France are backing a $1B space-AI infrastructure play.
themes.angle: War resilience is now a pricing factor in Gulf AI deals — contracts and risk models must treat strikes as a recurrence risk, not a one-off.

themes.title: Frontier research: self-improving AI and forecasting

themes.angle: The frontier is moving toward self-modification and forecasting parity — capability curves boards should track, not just product launches.
